title: kgfq receipt (C6, D5, D17)
description: Attached to every table as a sidecar and in the Parquet footer under `kgfq.receipt`, and written as a sidecar alone for a step that produced no table (a SPARQL run aborted at a budget). What makes an approximate answer a finding rather than a bug. Version 2 adds kind `sparql`: multiple graded sources, the query as run, the lint and normalization record, the engine's outcome and budget, requests folded by shape, and a pointer to the engine's own receipt in place of a copy of its request list. Version 3 reads `completeness` from what the client did with each response that carried the table's rows, not from the server's per-page flag: a page limit or a budget interruption (`time_budget`, `response_bytes`) whose cursor was followed no longer makes a table incomplete, and a read stopped with rows left (`max_rows`) always does. It adds `completeness.incomplete_because` and each request's `continued` and `stopped`.

step.description: The log step that produced the table.

grade.description: D17 source grade; a derived table takes the minimum over its inputs, a `sparql` run the minimum over its sources.

source.description: For grade `bundle`: the graph at its pinned release and the origin it was fetched from.

sources.description: For kind `sparql`: every source the engine was given, each graded — a bundle graph at its pinned release (`kgf`) or a SPARQL endpoint named explicitly (`sparql`).

url.description: The fragment URL of the pinned release, or the endpoint.

query.description: For kind `sparql`: the query text as run, verbatim.

original_query.description: The text as given, when `--normalize` changed it.

normalizations.description: One record per rewrite `--normalize` considered: applied or not, and why.

lint.description: The linter's threshold and every diagnostic over the query as run.

engine.description: For kind `sparql`: the engine's own versions (`kgf_sparql`, `comunica`, `node`), the command line as run, and its exit code.

budget.description: The plan-level budget the run was given: `max_requests`, `max_bytes`, `max_rows`, `timeout_s` (null = unlimited), and the engine's `max_connections`.

outcome.description: The engine's outcome verbatim: `contract` is `complete` (the output is exactly the solution set), `aborted` (with `budget`, the one that ended it) or `error` (with `error`); `rows` written; `result_type` bindings, quads or boolean.

plan.description: The kgfq.plan/1 document that was executed.

requests.description: Every request the library made, for kinds it makes itself. A `sparql` receipt does not copy the engine's list (see `requests_by_shape` and `engine_receipt`).

request_id.description: The server's KGF-Request-Id, for the access-log census.

continued.description: The client followed this response's cursor.

stopped.description: The read ended at this response while the server still had rows — the rest of the page, a cursor not followed, a bindings chunk not sent — and why (`max_rows`).

rows.description: Rows this response carried; null for a response that carried none of the table's (a `/count`, a `/schema` page).

requests_by_shape.description: For kind `sparql`: the engine's request list folded by method, route, bound positions, predicate and whether bindings were pushed — counts, bytes, time and statuses per shape, most requests first.

engine_receipt.description: For kind `sparql`: where the engine's receipt (`kgf-sparql.receipt/1`, every request with its id) is filed, relative to the workspace, and its digest.

statistics.description: For kind `sparql`: whether VoID statistics were on and how many `/schema` requests planning cost.

completeness.description: Read from the responses that carried the table's rows; the plan's `/count` and the statistics' `/schema` pages are evidence for the plan, not the table. For kind `sparql`, the engine's contract.

complete.description: False only when the read left rows the server still had: it stopped at a response with rows remaining, or a response said `complete: false` and was not a `page_limit`, `time_budget` or `response_bytes` whose cursor was followed (doc 03 §3.6: a cursor resumes with no loss).

incomplete_because.description: Why the table is incomplete: a client stop (`max_rows`), a server truncation not continued, or for kind `sparql` the budget that ended the run or `error`. Empty when complete.

truncation_reasons.description: Every truncation reason those responses gave, continued or not: the trace. `page_limit` here with `complete: true` is a paged read followed to its end; so is a continued `time_budget` or `response_bytes`.

approximations.description: Every approximation made, in words (R3 limit pushdown, a row budget, etc.).

statement.description: For kind `derived`: the SQL that produced the table.

content_hash.description: sha256 over the canonically sorted rows; order-independent.
